label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
**Renee, and anyone else reading this — thank you for letting me answer.** I'm the owner of Lotus Garden Nails on Bellaire. I want to tell you what actually happened, because I don't think you were dealt with fairly, but I also don't want to fight with you in a forum where nobody can see each other's faces.

Mrs. Meyerland, I'm sorry your toe hurt. I mean that. I read your post and I felt terrible for you. Nobody should leave a salon and get hurt.

**Who did your pedicure.** On Saturday, October 24, you had a deluxe pedicure, $45. Your technician was my niece, Vy. She has been licensed three years. She was born in Houston and she speaks English just fine — she is simply shy, and I'm sorry that came across as something else. She is not careless, and she cares about this work more than anything.

**Our sanitation.** Every instrument that touched your feet came out of the autoclave, and the sealed pouches were opened in front of you. Your file and buffer were brand new for your visit, and I believe you took them home with you. We put a fresh plastic liner in the foot tub for every customer, every time. If you have been in the salon, you may have noticed our state inspection certificate on the wall — we were inspected in August of this year and passed with no violations. You are always welcome to come in and look at it, or to ask anyone from the state.

**The cuticle.** During your pedicure you asked Vy to keep cutting, and she told you not too much, and you said that was fine because you always have it done that way. I'm not blaming you for that. I'm telling you because I would rather be honest than comfortable.

**What I offered.** When you came back on November 2 and showed me your red toe, I offered you your full $45 back, plus payment for your urgent care copay if you brought me the receipt. **That offer is still open.** It has not changed and it will not change. You asked for $300 cash and free pedicures for a year, and I said no. One customer's request is not a way a salon can run, and I hope you can see it from my side. But $45 back plus your copay is a real offer, made in good faith, and I stand by it.

**One thing I do need to say.** If I seemed like I shrugged at you, I am sorry. That was not what I intended, and I've thought about that since. What hurt me most in this thread is not your post — it's when people say all nail salons are dirty, like we're all the same. I've been in Houston 19 years. I opened this salon in 2007 right after I finished working for my aunt. In all that time I have never had an infection complaint, not once. My whole life is this work. My niece read your post and cried all night and told me she wants to leave the nail business. She is young and this is all she knows how to do.

**Marisol — thank you.** You wrote something kind and fair, and you gave me a reason to answer instead of hiding. You've been coming to us about four years and I appreciate you, and I appreciate you speaking up.

Renee, you filed with the state, and that's your right, and our inspection record is on the wall for anyone who wants to see it. But I'd ask you to please **call the salon and ask for me by name**, or come in and sit down with me. I'd much rather settle this face to face than here, where everyone is guessing.

I'm not going to fight with you. You've been my customer for two years, and you still are my customer. I want you back in my chair, and I want your toe to heal.

— Lotus Garden Nails, Houston
